project.name: NeoBank Digital Onboarding & KYC (Phase 1)
project.description: Replace branch-based account opening with a mobile-first digital onboarding journey for resident individual customers and sole proprietors, including e-KYC, video KYC, sanctions/PEP screening, customer risk rating, enhanced due diligence and periodic re-KYC, integrated with the legacy core banking system.

documents.title: Interview - Head of Digital Product
documents.masked_text:
Interviewer: What is the goal of the new onboarding?
Priya: Today customers have to visit a branch and it takes 3 days to open an account.
We want customers to open an account fully digitally on the mobile app.
The onboarding journey must be completed within 5 minutes for a normal customer.
We need the onboarding to be fast and user-friendly so that drop-off falls below 20%.
Customers should be able to fetch their identity details from DigiLocker or Aadhaar e-KYC instead of typing them.
To keep it frictionless, onboarding should be approved automatically without manual review for every customer.
We want to delete customer data after 3 years to reduce storage cost.
Customers must be able to save a partially completed application and resume it within 7 days.
The app should support English and Hindi in phase 1.
Example from the pilot: customer Ravi Kumar, PAN <PAN_1>, mobile <PHONE_1>, email <EMAIL_1> was stuck for 2 days.
Releases should happen every two weeks because competitors change their journeys frequently.

documents.title: Email - KYC requirements from Compliance
documents.masked_text:
Subject: KYC must-haves for the digital onboarding project
Team,
The system must screen every applicant against UN, domestic and internal sanctions lists before the account is opened.
All customers must be screened for PEP status and PEP relationships must be approved by a senior compliance officer.
The system shall assign every customer a low, medium or high risk rating based on the approved risk-scoring model.
High-risk customers must be manually reviewed and go through enhanced due diligence with source of funds evidence.
Periodic re-KYC must be scheduled every 2 years for high-risk, 8 years for medium-risk and 10 years for low-risk customers.
KYC records must be retained for at least 5 years after the account is closed.
KYC records of new customers must be uploaded to CKYCR within the regulatory timeline.
Where video KYC is used, the session must include liveness check, geo-tagging and face match by a trained official, and the recording must be stored securely.
Staff must be able to escalate suspicious applications to the Principal Officer for STR filing without alerting the customer.
Regards, Arjun

documents.title: Meeting notes - Information security review
documents.masked_text:
Information security review - onboarding
All identity documents and Aadhaar numbers must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 with keys in the HSM.
All traffic must use TLS 1.2 or higher.
Customers must log in with OTP plus device binding
staff must use MFA to access the back-office.
Aadhaar numbers must be masked in all screens, showing only the last 4 digits.
The system must keep a tamper-evident audit trail of every KYC decision and every access to customer documents.
The platform should be secure and robust against attacks.

documents.title: Interview - KYC operations lead
documents.masked_text:
Interviewer: How does KYC operations work today?
Rahul: Currently our team manually checks about 4,000 applications a day from branches, and the backlog is often 2 days.
Any manual override of an automated KYC decision must go through maker-checker approval with a reason.
Potential sanctions matches need a case management queue where analysts can review evidence and close alerts with comments.
We need the review queue to show cases sorted by risk and SLA age.
Ops needs a daily MIS report of applications approved, rejected and pending, by channel.
If the e-KYC vendor is down, applications should be queued and customers notified, not rejected.
Customer data must be retained for 10 years after the account is closed.

documents.title: Architecture constraints - legacy CBS
documents.masked_text:
Architecture constraints
The legacy core banking system only creates accounts through a nightly batch file
real-time account creation is not available until the CBS upgrade next year.
The onboarding platform must integrate with the core banking system through an asynchronous adapter and report account status back to the customer.
The onboarding APIs must handle a peak of 200 applications per minute during campaigns.
The onboarding service must have 99.9% monthly availability with an RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 15 minutes.
All integrations with vendors (e-KYC, video KYC, screening) must go through the API gateway.

documents.title: Customer research summary
documents.masked_text:
Customer research summary (n=40)
Customers want to know what is happening
the app should show clear progress and the reason if an application is rejected.
Customers expect the selfie step to work in low light and on older Android phones.
Customers want to be able to contest a rejection and talk to a human.
Several customers said they do not want their data used for marketing without asking them.

documents.title: Internal audit finding IA-2025-14
documents.masked_text:
Internal audit finding IA-2025-14 (High)
Sample testing found 12 accounts where the risk rating was changed manually without documented approval.
Recommendation: the new system must record who changed a customer risk rating, when, and why, and the change must be approved by a second user.
Consent for data processing was not recorded for 3% of sampled customers
the new system must capture and store explicit consent before collecting personal data.

risks.title: Legacy core-banking integration
risks.description: Account creation depends on legacy core banking interfaces (batch windows, limited APIs) that may break real-time onboarding targets.
risks.mitigation: Spike in sprint 1; asynchronous account creation with status callbacks; contract tests against a CBS simulator.

risks.title: Verification-vendor dependency
risks.description: Outage or degradation of identity, screening or registry vendors stops onboarding.
risks.mitigation: Dual-vendor strategy or graceful queueing; vendor SLAs and exit plan; circuit breakers.

risks.title: Biometric data breach
risks.description: Compromise of face images or templates is irreversible for customers.
risks.mitigation: Template protection, encryption with HSM keys, minimal retention, DPIA.

risks.title: Ambiguous or untestable requirements
risks.description: 10 requirements are vague or incomplete, which risks scope creep and failed UAT.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the clarification questions before the baseline gate.

risks.title: Automated adverse decisions without human review
risks.description: Fully automated rejection may breach automated-decision rules and fairness expectations.
risks.mitigation: Human review for rejections; reason codes; contest channel.
